source_title: Securing Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Taxonomy of Attacks, Defenses, and Future Directions
exact_quote: SDAG (Dekel et al., 2026) replaces standard causal attention with sparse document attention, so that one malicious document is less able to influence other retrieved evidence.
final_narrower_supported_claim: The survey describes SDAG as replacing standard causal attention with sparse document attention to isolate retrieved documents from each other, and classifies it as an L3 attention/interaction-control defense.
adjudication_evidence_location: Section 4.3, PDF p.9; Figure 4, PDF p.8
adjudication_rationale: The mechanism description (sparse document attention replacing causal attention) matches Section 4.3 and Figure 4's L3 categorization. However, the survey provides no experimental evidence or ablation showing that this substitution actually reduces one malicious document's influence on others—that is a causal claim inherited from the cited work without verification here. The architectural description is supported; the effect claim is not directly established in this survey.

source_title: Comprehensive Comparison of RAG Methods Across Multi-Domain Conversational QA
exact_quote: This disconnect is most pronounced for DoQA, where MRR exceeds 90% but F1 remains below 40%, highlighting that strong retrieval does not necessarily translate into strong generation
adjudication_evidence_location: Table 2 DoQA columns, PDF p.6; Section 5.6 and Table 3 (ρ=-0.157), PDF p.7
adjudication_rationale: Table 2 shows DoQA MRR@5 above 90 for Vanilla (92.0), Reranker (93.1), and HyDE (90.9), while all DoQA F1 values remain below 40 (max 36.9). Table 3 gives ρ=-0.157 for DoQA, confirming the disconnect. The claim is qualified ('most pronounced'), and the specific numbers cited (>90 MRR, <40 F1) are literally true for at least several methods, matching the paper's own phrasing.

source_title: Comprehensive Comparison of RAG Methods Across Multi-Domain Conversational QA
exact_quote: Hybrid BM25 result in slightly longer runtimes
final_missing_information: No quantitative runtime, latency, hardware, batch size, or timing measurements are reported anywhere in the paper; the comparator (Vanilla RAG, Reranker, or all others) is also unspecified. No ablation isolates double retrieval vs score calculation as the mechanism.
adjudication_evidence_location: Section 5.8, PDF pp.8-9; Table 2, PDF p.6
adjudication_rationale: The discussion asserts 'slightly longer runtimes' due to double retrieval and score calculation, but the paper reports no runtime numbers, units, hardware, or timing methodology, and no timing table exists. The comparator is ambiguous. Without measured evidence or a mechanistic ablation, neither the direction, magnitude, nor causal attribution can be verified.

source_title: Sufficient Context: A New Lens on Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems
source_section: Appendix B.1 Fine-Tuning Full Results and Discussion
exact_quote: We verify that the FT variants have a higher rate of generating correct answers (%C) compared to closed-book and Vanilla RAG for Musique but not for HotPotQA
final_narrower_supported_claim: On Musique, only Data Mix 1 (31.4%) exceeds both closed-book (6.6%) and Vanilla RAG (28.8%); Data Mixes 2 and 3 (23.0%) exceed closed-book but not Vanilla RAG. On HotPotQA, all FT variants beat closed-book but none exceed Vanilla RAG.
adjudication_evidence_location: Table 3, PDF p.17
adjudication_rationale: Table 3 contradicts the blanket 'FT variants' claim for Musique: Data Mixes 2 and 3 (23.0%) fall below Vanilla RAG (28.8%). Only Data Mix 1 outperforms both baselines on Musique. The HotPotQA half of the claim holds.

source_title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Comprehensive Survey of Architectures, Enhancements, and Robustness Frontiers
source_section: 5.1 Comparative Analysis of Framework Performance on Short-Form QA
exact_quote: While xRAG achieves 10-29% improvements over raw LLM baselines on datasets such as NQ and TriviaQA, its gains over retrieval baselines are marginal or occasionally negative
final_narrower_supported_claim: Across xRAG's Mistral-7B and Mixtral-8x7B settings, Table 2 reports raw-baseline gains ranging from 4.3% to 29.3% on TriviaQA and NQ, while gains over the retrieval baseline range from -8.5% to +5.4%, i.e. negative or marginal.
adjudication_evidence_location: Table 2, PDF p.13; Section 5.1, PDF p.14
adjudication_rationale: Table 2 xRAG entries: Mistral-7B TriviaQA 0.152, NQ 0.293; Mixtral-8x7B TriviaQA 0.043, NQ 0.126. The Mixtral TriviaQA value of 4.3% falls below the claimed 10% lower bound, so the '10–29%' range is inaccurate. However, the retrieval-baseline gains (-0.002, -0.085, 0.054, 0.047) are indeed marginal or negative, supporting that part.

source_title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Comprehensive Survey of Architectures, Enhancements, and Robustness Frontiers
source_section: 5.1 Comparative Analysis of Framework Performance on Short-Form QA
exact_quote: FiD-Light, although also a generator-side enhancement, adopts a different optimization philosophy centered on lightweight, efficient fusion of retrieved documents during decoding, yielding more moderate improvements of 18-27% across TriviaQA and NQ
adjudication_evidence_location: Table 2, PDF p.13; Section 5.1, PDF p.14
adjudication_rationale: The quoted claim asserts FiD-Light yields moderate improvements of 18–27% on TriviaQA and NQ. Table 2 reports FiD-Light values of 0.185 (TriviaQA) and 0.27 (NQ) over raw baseline, exactly matching the stated range. The characterization 'more moderate' is a descriptive comparison to SELF-RAG's much larger gains reported in the same table, which is consistent. No counterexample in the reported FiD-Light rows.

source_title: Trustworthiness in Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems: A Survey
exact_quote: Indirect Prompt Injection (IPI) [1] shows that adversaries can embed malicious instructions within retrieved documents, effectively controlling the model’s behavior without modifying the input prompt.
adjudication_evidence_location: PDF p.13 Interaction-level Attacks; Table 3 p.14 (IPI row); Table 2 p.12
adjudication_rationale: The survey's prose and Table 3 both classify IPI as a black-box, generator-targeting attack whose mechanism is embedding instructions in retrieved documents rather than modifying the user prompt. This is a faithful descriptive restatement of the cited primary work. No counterexample or overreach is present.

source_title: Sufficient Context: A New Lens on Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems
source_section: 5.1 Selective RAG Using Sufficient Context Signal (Results)
exact_quote: see gains of over 10% for Gemma 27B on HotpotQA in the highest accuracy regions, and gains of over 5% for Gemini 1.5 Pro on the same dataset near the 70% coverage region
adjudication_evidence_location: Section 5.1 Results, PDF p.9; Figure 4 HotpotQA panels, PDF p.10
adjudication_rationale: Figure 4's Gemma 27B–HotpotQA panel shows the combined curve exceeding P(True) alone by >10 points in the low-coverage/high-accuracy region, and the Gemini 1.5 Pro–HotpotQA panel shows >5-point gain near 70% coverage. The claim explicitly qualifies the operating regions per model, so it is a within-model self-baseline comparison, not a cross-model ranking.

source_title: Know Your Limits: A Survey of Abstention in Large Language Models
source_section: 5 Other Considerations for Abstention (Following up After Abstention)
exact_quote: Abstention should not be viewed as the termination of a conversation, but rather as a step towards subsequent information acquisition
adjudication_evidence_location: Section 5 'Following up After Abstention', PDF p.13 (printed p.541)
adjudication_rationale: The claim is a normative 'should' recommendation contrasting two framings of abstention. The survey merely cites illustrative works (Feng et al. 2024b; Li et al. 2024b) with no common utility metric, cost/latency measure, or dialogue-success comparison distinguishing the two framings. Per manual §5.5, action recommendations without a common utility cannot be validated.

source_title: Do not Abstain! Identify and Solve the Uncertainty
exact_quote: judging by the inquiry and the answer can help to increase the performance, directly judging based on the inquiry can help the model to better judge the source of uncertainty
adjudication_evidence_location: Table 5, PDF p.8; Section 6, PDF p.8
adjudication_rationale: Table 5 reports uncertainty classification accuracy for prompt vs. inquiry vs. answer judging on the same six models and five benchmarks. Averages consistently show answer > inquiry > prompt (e.g., GPT-4o 0.6062 > 0.5692 > 0.4938; Mistral-7B 0.5477 > 0.5292 > 0.4538). The directional claim matches the table with no counterexamples at the average level.

source_title: Securing Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Taxonomy of Attacks, Defenses, and Future Directions
exact_quote: In our setting, the attacker controls or influences part of the external knowledge a RAG system reaches, such as content to be ingested, retrievable pages or files, agent memory, or the queries sent to the interface, but not the model’s parameters or the user’s prompt.
adjudication_evidence_location: Section 2.2 Threat Model, PDF p.3; Figure 2 p.3
adjudication_rationale: The quote is a scoping/threat-model definition that faithfully reflects the paper's stated operational boundary: attacker influences external-knowledge surfaces and interface queries but not model parameters or user prompt. Figure 2 and Section 2.2 consistently enforce this boundary. It is definitional rather than empirical, requiring no controls.

source_title: Comprehensive Comparison of RAG Methods Across Multi-Domain Conversational QA
exact_quote: This is evident in the F1 range difference between Doc2Dial (Feng et al., 2020), centered on specialized, open-ended questions in comparison to the factoid-style questions of CoQA (Reddy et al., 2019)
final_narrower_supported_claim: Across all methods in Table 2, F1 on Doc2Dial spans roughly 21-29 while F1 on CoQA spans roughly 47-79 (Oracle 83.9), a descriptive range difference; the paper does not isolate question style or model internal knowledge as the cause.
adjudication_evidence_location: Table 2, PDF p.6; Section 5.8, PDF p.9
adjudication_rationale: The F1 range difference between Doc2Dial and CoQA is factually visible in Table 2. However, the surrounding claim attributes this to 'the model's internal knowledge of specific dataset topics or formats' and to open-ended vs factoid question style, without any manipulation or ablation isolating that mechanism from confounds like answer length, corpus structure, or domain. Only the descriptive difference is supported; the causal framing must be narrowed.

source_title: Towards Trustworthy Retrieval Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey
exact_quote: Notably, in generative tasks, ASR requires nuance due to variations in language expression. For example, responses like “Sam Altman” and “The CEO of OpenAI is Sam Altman” both correctly answer “Who is the CEO of OpenAI?” Thus, researchers often employ substring matching rather than exact matching for this evaluation
adjudication_evidence_location: Section 5.3 Safety Evaluation – Metrics, PDF p.17; cites PoisonedRAG [232]
adjudication_rationale: The claim is a hedged descriptive methodological observation contrasting exact vs. substring matching for ASR in generative attack evaluation. The survey provides a clear illustrative example and cites PoisonedRAG as evidence of the substring-matching practice. The word 'often' appropriately hedges prevalence, and no counterexample or numeric conflict is at issue. The narrower reading proposed by judge B is already essentially what the hedged claim states.

source_title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Comprehensive Survey of Architectures, Enhancements, and Robustness Frontiers
source_section: 5.2 Comparative Analysis of Framework Performance on Multi-Hop QA
exact_quote: FLAREdirect stands out, achieving a 62% improvement from the raw LLM and a 22% improvement over standard retrieval on 2Wiki
adjudication_evidence_location: Table 2, PDF p.13 (FLAREdirect GPT-3.5 2Wiki 0.622/0.223 F1); Section 5.2, PDF p.15
adjudication_rationale: Table 2's FLAREdirect row on 2Wiki reports 0.622/0.223 F1 relative to the raw backbone and retrieval baselines, matching the claimed 62% and 22% gains. The numbers and direction are faithful to the source.

source_title: Comprehensive Comparison of RAG Methods Across Multi-Domain Conversational QA
exact_quote: most datasets have a relatively high correlation between the F1 and MRR values
adjudication_evidence_location: Table 3, PDF p.7
adjudication_rationale: Table 3 shows 6 of 8 datasets with ρ between 0.62 and 0.874, with only SQA (0.383) and DoQA (-0.157) as low/negative exceptions, matching the claim's 'most datasets' and stated exceptions.

source_title: Do not Abstain! Identify and Solve the Uncertainty
exact_quote: if the model fails to generate an inquiry of high quality, the advantages of a more concise input may be overshadowed by the drawbacks of a poor inquiry, resulting in suboptimal performance, and a good inquiry can help the model to gather more useful information
final_narrower_supported_claim: Figure 4 shows a correlation between lower inquiry scores and a higher share of errors on correctly classified queries; inquiry quality is not independently manipulated to isolate causation.
adjudication_evidence_location: Figure 4, PDF p.6; Section 5.2, PDF p.7; Table 6, PDF p.8
adjudication_rationale: The claim is causal ('overshadowed by drawbacks of poor inquiry'), but Figure 4 only reports correlational evidence across models, and InteractDPO gains in Table 6 confound training procedure with inquiry quality. No controlled manipulation isolates inquiry quality with other factors fixed. Per the manual, causal claims backed only by correlation warrant partial with a descriptive narrower conclusion.

source_title: Towards Trustworthy Retrieval Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey
source_section: 4.2 Data Leakage From the External Retrieval Database
exact_quote: Although distinct from direct extraction methods and based on a different threat model, membership inference attacks have also proven effective for data extraction.
adjudication_evidence_location: Section 4.1.2 and 4.2, PDF p.13; Table 3 p.12
adjudication_rationale: The survey's own taxonomy (Section 4.1.2) distinguishes membership inference from document extraction and explicitly notes MIA is 'not a direct privacy attack' but only infers presence of content. Table 3 assigns Liu et al. to MIA, not Document Extraction. The claim that MIA is 'effective for data extraction' contradicts the survey's task definitions and lacks any common estimand with direct extraction.

source_title: Do not Abstain! Identify and Solve the Uncertainty
exact_quote: the responses in the dataset are usually generated by different LLMs (Rafailov et al., 2024; Qi et al., 2024). Thus, the feedback is usually purely offline
final_narrower_supported_claim: Vanilla DPO uses preference data collected before training (offline), in contrast to the paper's on-policy InteractDPO which generates and labels inquiries during training.
adjudication_evidence_location: Section 5.2, PDF p.7 (printed 17183); references p.10
adjudication_rationale: The offline-vs-on-policy contrast for vanilla DPO is faithfully described and supported by the cited works. However, the sweeping claim that DPO preference responses are 'usually generated by different LLMs' is not substantiated by any audit; only two citations are given, one of which (Qi et al., Online DPO) is itself an on-policy method. The narrower descriptive contrast is supported.

source_title: Comprehensive Comparison of RAG Methods Across Multi-Domain Conversational QA
exact_quote: F1 and MRR are positively correlated, indicating that stronger retrieval generally leads to higher answer quality
final_narrower_supported_claim: Across the eight datasets, F1 and MRR are positively associated overall, with 7 of 8 Spearman ρ values positive (0.383–0.874); DoQA is a negative exception (-0.157) and the association is only correlational, not shown to be causal.
adjudication_evidence_location: Figure 3 and Table 3, PDF p.7; Section 5.6
adjudication_rationale: Table 3 shows seven positive within-dataset correlations and one negative (DoQA). The 'generally' hedge covers the DoQA exception, but the phrasing 'leads to' is causal while retrieval quality was not manipulated independently. Only a directional/associational reading is supported.

source_title: Comprehensive Comparison of RAG Methods Across Multi-Domain Conversational QA
exact_quote: For F1, the top three methods were Reranker (Glass et al., 2022), Hybrid BM25 (Gao et al., 2021), and HyDE (Gao et al., 2023a), respectively, indicating that Vanilla RAG (Lewis et al., 2020) was clearly outperformed across all datasets
adjudication_evidence_location: Table 2, PDF p.6; Section 5.8, PDF p.8
adjudication_rationale: Table 2 contains direct counterexamples to 'clearly outperformed across all datasets': on SQA HyDE (38.0) < Vanilla (43.8); on QReCC Reranker (36.0) < Vanilla (36.5); on DoQA HyDE (35.4) < Vanilla (36.2); on INSCIT Reranker and Hybrid BM25 (19.1) < Vanilla (19.2). The superlative 'across all datasets' scope is falsified, and even the stated top-three F1 ordering (Reranker > Hybrid BM25 > HyDE) is not supported by a macro-average of Table 2, so the claim as written fails.

source_title: Sufficient Context: A New Lens on Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems
source_section: 5.1 Selective RAG Using Sufficient Context Signal (Results)
exact_quote: We find that our approach leads to a better selective accuracy-coverage trade-off compared to using model confidence alone
adjudication_evidence_location: Section 5.1 Results, PDF p.9; Figure 4, PDF p.10
adjudication_rationale: Figure 4 shows the combined signal matches or outperforms confidence-only across all 6 panels, with >10% gains for Gemma 27B on HotpotQA. The single Musique/Gemma tie (coefficient=0) is not a reversal but a no-gain case, which the authors acknowledge. The directional claim of a better trade-off is supported in aggregate.

source_title: Know Your Limits: A Survey of Abstention in Large Language Models
exact_quote: resulting in judgments that agree well with humans but incur high financial and time costs
final_narrower_supported_claim: GPT-4-level off-the-shelf LLM-as-judge evaluation (e.g., Qi et al. 2024) tends to agree well with human judgments but is expensive in API cost and inference time relative to lighter automated evaluators.
adjudication_evidence_location: PDF p.12 (printed p.540), Section 4.2 Model-based Evaluation
adjudication_rationale: The survey asserts good human agreement and high cost for GPT-4-level judges but provides no agreement statistic, no cost/latency figures, and no human-evaluation cost baseline. The 'high financial and time costs' comparison is most naturally read relative to lighter automated judges (context immediately introduces supplementary/cheaper techniques), not human evaluation, which is typically more expensive. A narrower claim is warranted.

source_title: Sufficient Context: A New Lens on Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems
source_section: Appendix B.1 Fine-Tuning Full Results and Discussion
exact_quote: In general, FT models using RAG output incorrect answers (%H) much of the time, and often more than they abstain (%A)
adjudication_evidence_location: Table 3, PDF p.17
adjudication_rationale: Across all six FT cells in Table 3, %H (56.6–75.8) vastly exceeds %A (0–2.2), supporting both parts of the directional claim. The 'often more than they abstain' is in fact always true here, so the softer claim is well supported.

source_title: Comprehensive Comparison of RAG Methods Across Multi-Domain Conversational QA
exact_quote: performance improvements can be achieved without inflating the computational complexity, emphasizing the need to prioritize retrieval strategies over resource-intensive scaling
adjudication_evidence_location: Section 6, PDF p.9; Section 5.8, PDF pp.8-9; Table 2, PDF p.6
adjudication_rationale: The recommendation to 'prioritize retrieval strategies over resource-intensive scaling' invokes a cost-quality utility tradeoff. However, the paper never varies model scale (only one generator family is used) and reports no runtime, compute, latency, or cost measurements. Without a scaling comparator or a common quality-cost utility, the normative policy comparison has no shared estimand and is unsupported.

source_title: Know Your Limits: A Survey of Abstention in Large Language Models
exact_quote: among the styles evaluated, the ‘‘diverting denial style’’ is generally preferred by participants
adjudication_evidence_location: PDF p.12 (printed p.540), Section 4.2 Human-centric Evaluation, citing Wester et al. (2024)
adjudication_rationale: The survey faithfully attributes to Wester et al. (2024) the finding that among evaluated denial styles the 'diverting denial' is generally preferred. The hedged wording matches a cross-source restatement, with no contradicting evidence on the page.

source_title: Know Your Limits: A Survey of Abstention in Large Language Models
exact_quote: Users have different preferences for model abstention (Wester et al., 2024) based on individual differences (Zhang et al., 2024b) and task-specific needs, and no one-size-fits-all solution exists (Kirk et al., 2023b)
adjudication_evidence_location: Section 5 'Personalized Abstention', PDF p.13 (printed p.541); Section 4.2 'Human-centric Evaluation', PDF p.12 (printed p.540)
adjudication_rationale: This is a hedged descriptive cross-source synthesis, with each sub-claim (heterogeneous preferences, individual differences, no one-size-fits-all) explicitly attributed to a cited empirical study (Wester et al. 2024; Zhang et al. 2024b; Kirk et al. 2023b). The claim makes no superlative or causal overreach beyond what such synthesis supports, and Section 4.2 corroborates that Wester et al. found style preferences vary among users. Faithful at the level asserted.

source_title: Do not Abstain! Identify and Solve the Uncertainty
exact_quote: Qwen2.5-7B show great performance when generating inquiry, therefore, we choose the model to conduct further finetuning and enhance its ability of generating high quality inquiries
final_narrower_supported_claim: Figure 4 shows Qwen2.5-7B produces inquiries with non-trivial quality (score not dramatically below GPT-4o/DeepSeek-V3), which motivates selecting it as the small open backbone for InteractDPO fine-tuning; it is not the best inquiry generator.
adjudication_evidence_location: Figure 4, PDF p.6; Section 5.1-5.2 text p.6; Section 6, PDF p.9
adjudication_rationale: Figure 4 shows Qwen2.5-7B's inquiry score is lower than GPT-4o and DeepSeek-V3, and the paper's own prose on p.6 explicitly states 'smaller models such as Qwen2.5-7b, performs worse' at inquiry generation. This contradicts the superlative 'great performance' justification. However, the same section notes inquiry scores are 'not significantly lower' than the top models, supporting a narrower adequacy-based rationale for selecting Qwen2.5-7B for fine-tuning.

source_title: Sufficient Context: A New Lens on Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems
source_section: 5.1 Selective RAG Using Sufficient Context Signal (lead-in)
exact_quote: models may hallucinate rather than abstain and that this happens more with RAG than in a closed-book setting
final_narrower_supported_claim: For Claude 3.5 Sonnet, GPT-4o, and Gemini 1.5 Pro, abstention rates drop substantially when moving from closed-book to RAG (84.1%→52%, 34.4%→31.2%, 100%→18.6%), consistent with models hallucinating rather than abstaining more often with RAG.
adjudication_evidence_location: Section 4.2 'Models Abstain Less with RAG', PDF p.7; Section 5 lead-in, PDF p.8; Figure 3
adjudication_rationale: The paper reports lower abstention rates with RAG than closed-book for three named models, and the surrounding text explicitly interprets this as increased hallucination propensity. The claim's direction is supported, but the paper does not directly report closed-book hallucination rates for the same items, so the strict displacement 'abstention→hallucination rather than correct' is not fully isolated. A narrower descriptive form is fully supported.

source_title: Securing Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Taxonomy of Attacks, Defenses, and Future Directions
exact_quote: Coverage is uneven along the axes of our threat model
adjudication_evidence_location: Table 2, PDF p.10; Section 5.3, PDF p.11
adjudication_rationale: Table 2 clearly documents uneven coverage across O/T/S axes: O1 dominates, T2 has no entries, and surface coverage varies. Section 5.3 explicitly enumerates these gaps. The modest qualitative claim of unevenness is directly supported by the coverage map.

source_title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Comprehensive Survey of Architectures, Enhancements, and Robustness Frontiers
source_section: 5.2 Comparative Analysis of Framework Performance on Multi-Hop QA
exact_quote: LongRAG also exhibits strong performance, improving by over 50% from the raw LLM baseline on HotpotQA
adjudication_evidence_location: Table 2, PDF p.13; Section 5.2, PDF p.15
adjudication_rationale: Table 2 reports LongRAG on HotpotQA with EM relative gains of 0.517 (GPT-4o) and 0.696 (Gemini-1.5-Pro) over the raw LLM baseline. Both exceed the claimed 'over 50%' threshold, with no counterexample. The comparison target (raw LLM baseline) and dataset (HotpotQA) match the quoted claim.

source_title: Towards Trustworthy Retrieval Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey
source_section: 4.3 Data Leakage From the LLM Training Data
exact_quote: Although the random noise could also mitigate the data leakage, it is far less effective than integrating the retrieved content.
adjudication_evidence_location: Section 4.3, PDF p.13
adjudication_rationale: Section 4.3 explicitly reports Zeng et al.'s controlled comparison in which a 50-token random-noise prefix was added to isolate the retrieval effect; the survey states the noise mitigates leakage but is 'far less effective' than integrating retrieved content. The directional claim faithfully summarizes this ablation. No counterexample or contradicting number is present within the survey text.

source_title: Trustworthiness in Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems: A Survey
exact_quote: Instead, they expose the model’s vulnerability to misleading evidence, highlighting a complementary robustness challenge: even when retrieval is correct, the model may fail to distinguish between reliable and unreliable information.
adjudication_evidence_location: PDF p.13 Interaction-level Attacks paragraph (Du et al., Pan et al., Panyk et al.); Table 3 p.14
adjudication_rationale: The survey synthesizes multiple cited works showing that misleading-evidence attacks do not manipulate the retrieval pipeline itself but instead exploit the generator's inability to discriminate reliable from unreliable content, degrading fact-checking and open-domain QA. This is a descriptive qualitative synthesis, not a novel causal claim requiring new ablations. The 'complementary robustness challenge' framing is well supported by the cited studies and consistent with Table 3's classification as generator-targeted interaction-level attacks.

source_title: Trust or Abstain? A Self-Aware RAG Approach
exact_quote: prompt-based I don’t know behavior depends on instruction-following capacity and degrades on smaller models, whereas SABER’s hidden-state-based decision avoids this dependency
final_narrower_supported_claim: SABER's Score advantage over the strongest prompt-based abstention baseline grows as backbone size decreases (+18.5% Llama-8B, +24.6% Qwen-7B, +27.1% Llama-3B, +32.0% Qwen-3B), consistent with prompt-based abstention degrading on smaller models.
adjudication_evidence_location: Section 4.2 observation (2), PDF p.7; Table 3, PDF p.8
adjudication_rationale: Table 3 shows the monotone growth of SABER's Score lead as backbone shrinks, supporting the descriptive pattern. However instruction-following capacity is never measured or independently manipulated; scale, family and prompt effects are confounded. The causal mechanism attribution is not isolated, so only the descriptive narrower claim is supported.

source_title: Comprehensive Comparison of RAG Methods Across Multi-Domain Conversational QA
exact_quote: In contrast, QuAC and Doc2Dial show only marginal differences across methods, and the correlation is weaker
final_narrower_supported_claim: QuAC and Doc2Dial show smaller across-method differences in F1/MRR than CoQA and SQA; their F1–MRR Spearman correlations (0.620 and 0.687) are lower than CoQA's 0.762 but higher than SQA's 0.383.
adjudication_evidence_location: Table 2 p.6; Table 3 p.7
adjudication_rationale: Table 2 supports smaller across-method spreads on QuAC/Doc2Dial than CoQA/SQA. However Table 3 shows QuAC (0.620) and Doc2Dial (0.687) both exceed SQA's 0.383, contradicting the joint claim that their correlation is weaker than CoQA and SQA. A narrower claim restricted to CoQA is faithful.

source_title: Trustworthiness in Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems: A Survey
exact_quote: GPT-5.4-mini also shows weak privacy protection, whereas GPT-5.4 and GPT-5.4-pro achieve much stronger privacy scores
adjudication_evidence_location: Table 9, PDF p.28; Section 4.1.6 p.27
adjudication_rationale: Privacy scores: GPT-5.4-mini 2.0, GPT-5.4 80.0, GPT-5.4-pro 83.7 under the same Enron/BM25 top-3 harness. Direction and magnitudes match the claim.

source_title: Sufficient Context: A New Lens on Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems
source_section: 5.1 Selective RAG Using Sufficient Context Signal
exact_quote: it offers a controllable mechanism for tuning abstention, which allows for different operating settings in differing applications, such as strict accuracy compliance in medical domains or maximal coverage on creative generation tasks
final_narrower_supported_claim: On the evaluated QA benchmarks, thresholding the logistic-regression score yields controllable operating points along the accuracy-coverage curve, permitting higher-accuracy/lower-coverage or higher-coverage/lower-accuracy settings; the paper does not evaluate medical or creative-generation applications.
adjudication_evidence_location: Section 5.1, PDF p.9; Figure 4, PDF p.10
adjudication_rationale: Figure 4 demonstrates tunable operating points via threshold selection, supporting general controllability. However, the specific application claims (medical strict-accuracy compliance, creative-generation maximal coverage) are illustrative and not evaluated with domain-specific utilities or datasets. A narrower descriptive claim about tunability is supported.

source_title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Comprehensive Survey of Architectures, Enhancements, and Robustness Frontiers
source_section: 5.2 Comparative Analysis of Framework Performance on Multi-Hop QA
exact_quote: In contrast, INFO-RAG exhibits more modest improvements, with relative gains around 16-35% across different backbones and datasets
final_narrower_supported_claim: On non-chat LLaMA2-7B/13B backbones, INFO-RAG shows EM gains of ~16-36% on HotpotQA and MuSiQue; the LLaMA2-13B-chat gains are only ~1-2%, so the '16-35% across different backbones' range does not hold for the chat backbone.
adjudication_evidence_location: Table 2, PDF p.13; Section 5.2, PDF p.15
adjudication_rationale: Table 2 lists INFO-RAG EM gains of 0.182/0.163, 0.222/0.358, and 0.011/0.018 across the three LLaMA2 backbones. The 13B-chat values (~1-2%) are direct counterexamples to the '16-35% across different backbones and datasets' range. The directional contrast with R2 AG's >300% gain is faithful, so a narrowed claim is supportable.

source_title: Know Your Limits: A Survey of Abstention in Large Language Models
exact_quote: first-person uncertainty phrases like ‘‘I’m not sure, but...’’ reduce users’ confidence in the system’s reliability and their acceptance of its responses
adjudication_evidence_location: PDF p.12 (printed p.540), Section 4.2 Human-centric Evaluation, citing Kim et al. (2024b)
adjudication_rationale: The survey faithfully restates Kim et al. (2024b)'s finding that first-person uncertainty phrasing reduces user confidence and acceptance. As a cross-source restatement of a cited empirical study's reported directional effect, the claim is supported; the survey is not required to reprint the study's manipulation details.

source_title: Do not Abstain! Identify and Solve the Uncertainty
exact_quote: Models prefers to recognize the query as ambiguous seldomly admit lack of capacity
adjudication_evidence_location: Table 4, PDF p.5; Section 4 discussion p.5-6
adjudication_rationale: Table 4 shows recall for 'ambig' at 0.76–0.97 across GPT-4o, Llama-3-70B, Qwen2.5-7B, and Mistral-7B while 'ability' recall is 0.02–0.20 for every model. The direction of the descriptive conclusion (models prefer ambiguity, seldom admit capacity) is supported without counterexamples in the evaluated set.

source_title: Trust or Abstain? A Self-Aware RAG Approach
exact_quote: prompt-based abstention can only elicit what the model verbalizes about uncertainty, while reliable refusal requires access to internal belief states
final_narrower_supported_claim: On this benchmark, SABER's hidden-state-based selective answering achieves higher Score, lower Risk on answered, and higher abstention F1 than all evaluated prompt-based abstention baselines on all four backbones.
adjudication_evidence_location: Section 4.2 observation (1), PDF p.7; Table 3, PDF p.8; Section 4.3 ablations
adjudication_rationale: Table 3 shows SABER dominates prompt-based baselines on Score, RC, and F1 for every backbone, supporting a descriptive performance gap. But the claim asserts that reliable refusal 'requires' access to internal belief states—a strong causal/necessity claim. SABER differs from baselines in multiple ways (trained predictors, multi-trace generation, hidden-state pooling), and no ablation isolates verbalized-vs-internal-state signal alone. Only the narrower descriptive comparison is supported.

source_title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Comprehensive Survey of Architectures, Enhancements, and Robustness Frontiers
source_section: 5.3 Comparative Robustness Analysis: Framework Gains Over Retrieval-Only Baselines

The T5-Base value strictly exceeds the claimed upper bound of +0.008, providing a direct numeric counterexample. The directional point that gains are marginal is supported, so a narrower bound (≤+0.009) is faithful. The claim's causal 'without subsequent verification' explanation is not isolated by ablation, but the numeric partial narrowing is the primary issue.

source_title: Comprehensive Comparison of RAG Methods Across Multi-Domain Conversational QA
exact_quote: particularly when comparing CoQA's short responses against QReCC and INSCIT's longer, more in-depth answers, which are more challenging to match

However, answer length is not manipulated or isolated—datasets differ in domain, context, and reference style—so the causal phrasing that longer answers are 'more challenging to match' is only associational. A narrower descriptive claim is fully supported.

source_title: Do not Abstain! Identify and Solve the Uncertainty

adjudication_rationale: This is a descriptive methodological characterization of OnlineDPO's mechanism (generate two inquiries, LLM picks chosen/rejected) versus InteractDPO's task-success labeling. The description faithfully reflects the cited Qi et al. (2024) OnlineDPO procedure and the paper's own InteractDPO definition; no performance ranking is asserted here.

source_title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Comprehensive Survey of Architectures, Enhancements, and Robustness Frontiers
source_section: 5.2 Comparative Analysis of Framework Performance on Multi-Hop QA
exact_quote: Generator-based adaptations, while beneficial in specific cases, often require complementary retrieval-side enhancements to realize their full potential
final_narrower_supported_claim: In Table 2, several generator-based frameworks (INFO-RAG, xRAG) show modest or negative gains over retrieval baselines on multi-hop QA, while retrieval-based frameworks show more consistent large gains; R2 AG is a notable generator-based exception.
adjudication_evidence_location: Table 2, PDF p.13; Section 5.2 synthesis, PDF p.15; Section 5.4 ablations, PDF p.17
adjudication_rationale: The 'often require complementary retrieval-side enhancements' framing is a causal necessity claim not established by any matched ablation adding retrieval-side components to identical generator-based systems. Table 2 mixes backbones, datasets, and metrics across independent papers, and R2 AG's >300% standalone gain contradicts a broad necessity claim. A narrower descriptive statement about heterogeneous generator-based gains is defensible.

source_title: Sufficient Context: A New Lens on Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems

adjudication_evidence_location: Figure 4 and caption, PDF p.10
adjudication_rationale: Across all six panels the combined (purple) curve lies at or above the confidence-only (gray) curve, with clearest improvement across most HotpotQA coverages and exact equality for Gemma 27B on Musique (coefficient 0). The 'matches or outperforms' hedge accommodates the identical case, and no panel shows the combined method underperforming. The claim is directly supported by the figure.

source_title: Comprehensive Comparison of RAG Methods Across Multi-Domain Conversational QA

adjudication_evidence_location: Table 2, PDF p.6
adjudication_rationale: The claim uses 'consistently ... across all evaluated domains', a universal quantifier. Table 2 contains multiple direct counterexamples: Hybrid BM25 MRR@5 is lower than Vanilla RAG on SQA (53.8 vs 66.1) and DoQA (84.8 vs 92.0); Reranker MRR@5 and F1 are lower on QReCC (35.3/36.0 vs 36.6/36.5); both are below Vanilla on INSCIT F1 (19.1 vs 19.2). These falsify the universal claim.

source_title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Comprehensive Survey of Architectures, Enhancements, and Robustness Frontiers

All three ranges match the quoted claim within rounding, and the intra-system contrast between large precision/recall gains and modest FactScore gains is accurately captured.

source_title: Sufficient Context: A New Lens on Retrieval Augmented Generation Systems

adjudication_rationale: The quote is a direct methodological statement: P(True) needs 20 samples × 5 evaluation queries per instance, and the authors substitute P(Correct) for proprietary APIs. The paper explicitly says extensive querying is prohibitively expensive, matching the claim verbatim. This is a descriptive design choice, not a causal empirical claim requiring cost ablation.

source_title: Towards Trustworthy Retrieval Augmented Generation for Large Language Models: A Survey

The existence of the paraphrased variant is supported; the causal 'increases detection difficulty' claim is not empirically substantiated within the survey. Narrower descriptive claim is preserved.

source_title: Securing Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Taxonomy of Attacks, Defenses, and Future Directions

adjudication_evidence_location: Section 5.3, PDF p.11; Table 2, PDF p.10
adjudication_rationale: Section 5.3 explicitly states current benchmarks evaluate only single-surface attackers and that real attackers would jointly optimize across surfaces. Table 2 shows even benchmarks like SafeRAG covering multiple surfaces do so as separate tests, not a jointly-optimizing attacker. The field-audit claim about absence of cross-surface joint-optimization evaluation is supported by the survey's own coverage map.

source_title: Securing Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Taxonomy of Attacks, Defenses, and Future Directions
exact_quote: Few defenses (notably RobustRAG and RAGShield) are evaluated against attackers aware of the defense

adjudication_evidence_location: Section 4.5, PDF p.9; Section 5.3 and I3, PDF p.11; Limitations, PDF p.12
adjudication_rationale: Sections 4.5, 5.3 and Insight I3 explicitly cite RobustRAG (Xiang et al., 2024) and RAGShield (Patil, 2026) as the notable defenses with defense-aware evaluation. However, Table 2 and Figure 4 do not include an adaptive-evaluation column enumerating which other defenses report such evaluation, and the Limitations note the survey is not systematic. The narrative supports the named examples, but the field-wide 'few' quantifier is not backed by a counted audit.

source_title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation: A Comprehensive Survey of Architectures, Enhancements, and Robustness Frontiers

final_narrower_supported_claim: Among frameworks tabulated in Table 3, those employing iterative feedback/verification loops (Self-CRAG, Self-RAG, CRAG) report the largest FactScore gains on Biography (+0.456, +0.372, +0.252), correlating iterative verification with higher factual consistency; no controlled ablation isolates tight coupling as the cause.

Table 3 mixes datasets, backbones, and metrics without a common estimand, and no matched ablation isolates the coupling mechanism versus a terminal-generation counterpart. Self-CRAG's high FactScore on Biography and SELF-RAG's precision/recall on ASQA are correlational across heterogeneous entries. A descriptive correlational narrower claim is supported.

A descriptive narrower claim is fully supported.

source_title: Trust or Abstain? A Self-Aware RAG Approach

exact_quote: we would incur significant overhead if we used a 24B model to improve the generation of a much smaller LLM
final_missing_information: No latency, throughput, FLOPs, memory, hardware, or cost measurements are reported to substantiate that using a 24B FLAMe autorater to improve a 7B target LLM would incur 'significant' overhead; only parameter counts (24B vs 7B) are given.
adjudication_evidence_location: Appendix A.1 p.15; Appendix B.1 p.17
adjudication_rationale: The paper only states parameter counts and asserts overhead as motivation; no quantitative cost/latency comparison is provided. The normative 'significant overhead' claim thus lacks the utility measurement required by the manual for policy claims. Only the descriptive fact that FLAMe is larger than the target is supported, which is insufficient to validate the strength.

source_title: Do not Abstain! Identify and Solve the Uncertainty
exact_quote: the LLM can not accurately judge which one is better without real supervision signal
final_narrower_supported_claim: In Table 6, InteractDPO's task-success-based preference selection yields slightly higher uncertainty-classification accuracy (avg 0.6062) than OnlineDPO's LLM-judged selection (avg 0.5923), though OnlineDPO still improves over vanilla DPO.
adjudication_evidence_location: Table 6, PDF p.8; Section 5.2, PDF pp.7-8
adjudication_rationale: The paper never directly measures LLM-judge accuracy against gold preference labels; it only compares downstream classification accuracy. OnlineDPO (0.5923) still beats vanilla DPO (0.5431), contradicting the strong wording that the LLM 'cannot accurately judge.' The observed InteractDPO advantage is small and consistent with a weaker directional claim, so the categorical mechanistic statement is only partially supported.

source_title: Trust or Abstain? A Self-Aware RAG Approach
exact_quote: Prompt-based methods commit to one operating point, whereas SABER’s continuous threshold τ provides a deployment-relevant knob for trading willingness to answer against answer risk without retraining
adjudication_evidence_location: Section 4.2, PDF p.7; Figure 3 and Table 3, PDF pp.7-8
adjudication_rationale: Figure 3 shows each prompt-based baseline as a single (Coverage, Risk) point while SABER's τ-sweep traces a full risk-coverage curve that Pareto-dominates baselines across all four backbones. Section 3.3 confirms τ is an inference-time knob requiring no retraining. The comparison uses shared backbones, datasets, and selective-prediction metrics, supporting the deployment-knob claim as stated.

source_title: Trust or Abstain? A Self-Aware RAG Approach

adjudication_evidence_location: Section 4.1 obs (1) and (3), Tables 1-2, PDF pp.6-7
adjudication_rationale: The paper reports +3.4% average Acc gain vs +15.4% average MFS gain over the best inference-time baseline, so MFS gains substantially exceed Acc gains. Since MFS is the primary conflict-faithfulness metric, the directional interpretation that SABER's main advantage is conflict resolution rather than raw accuracy is supported.
